text.text_excerpt: Recently, I made my first visit to New Orleans with my company for a conference and we stayed at this Sheraton right on Canal Street. Let me just say that there are a lot of good things going for this specific hotel! Coming to NOLA for the first time, I was really excited about the experience. In many ways, this hotel captures the spirit of the Crescent City. Right when you walk into Sheraton, you see a bunch of paintings of colorful dogs. There's also a grand piano in the lobby that seemingly presents itself as a metaphor for the musical soul of NOLA. If you go into the Gallery, there's also paintings that remind you of the South. The environment is totally set for your stay! Before this...

We Pricelined a hotel room and got the Sheraton New Orleans. It was going through a renovation remodel at the time of our stay which was kind of annoying. You could hear the construction going on from about 7am-7pm. Thankfully we weren't in the room too much during the day so it wasn't that bad. We got one of the newly renovated rooms and it was very nice. We had a huge King size bed that was very comfy... almost too comfy; we didn't want to get out of bed. The hotel has a Starbucks on the bottom floor which was always packed with people. They have shorter hours than a stand alone location, but if Starbucks is your thing, it's nice to have one in the hotel. The best thing about this hotel...

I'd say this Sheraton overall is a 3.5 or 4 star. You can't beat location! I somehow found a $100/night deal on Pricewire/some online booking site for a weekend right after New Years. I always thought staying in this part of town would cost me much more. We walked all over NOLA and only used Uber maybe 3x to places really far. It was great. Sheraton to most places are maybe a 15 min walk -- even at night time, I felt pretty safe since shops were open/lights were everywhere. Lobby - *There is a Sbux *There is a cool bar area *Quite a few TVs-- even on the wall using a projector. Football fans- you'll be happy. Drinking beer at the bar and watching a football on a huge screen? Hell yeah. So...
